title: Botswana's Diamonds: The De Beers Sale, a 30% Stake and the Slump | The Six, Ep. 16
lede: Botswana says it will double its stake in De Beers to 30% once Anglo American sells its 85% holding to a consortium led by former De Beers chief Gareth Penny. The deal comes after a diamond slump that shrank Botswana's economy in 2024 and 2025, and binding documents have not yet been signed.
keyPoints: On Nov. 9, 2026, President Duma Boko told parliament Botswana backs the sale of Anglo American's 85% stake to the Global Diamond Consortium and will raise its own stake from 15% to 30%, becoming De Beers' largest shareholder. Angola says it wants 10%; Namibia is reported to want the same (Reuters; AP).

Diamonds bring Botswana about a third of government revenue and about three-quarters of its foreign exchange. Debswana, a 50:50 venture with De Beers, mines about 90% of the country's diamonds (Reuters).
Debswana typically mined about 24 million carats a year before the downturn; it produced 15 million in 2025 and plans 18 million in 2026 (Reuters).

Botswana's economy shrank 2.8% in 2024 and 0.7% in 2025, then grew 8.7% year on year in the second quarter of 2026 as diamond output recovered. Public debt rose from 22% of GDP in 2023 to nearly 40% in 2025 (Statistics Botswana via Reuters; World Bank).

De Beers' average rough price index was 65 in the third quarter of 2026, down 20% from 81 a year earlier. A 2011 deal valued De Beers at almost $13 billion; Anglo cut its carrying value to $2.3 billion in February (De Beers; Bloomberg).
